title: Mission Power Level Ceiling
doc: CKF Hard Mode - mission Power Level ceiling.
MissionPowerLevel = round( (TeamPowerLevel + offset) * scalar )
clamped to [MinCap, MaxCap]
This section does the one thing the game's own difficulty sliders cannot:
lift the ceiling of 10 the game clamps its own result to. Everything else -
the offset and the scalar - is set on the sliders, and read back off the
same GameDifficultyModel instance the postfix is handed.
These are consts in PowerLevelCap.cs, not settings, because each is a
measured fact about the game:
Derived calls     pass through. arg0 was pinned to
max(1, Floor(teamPowerLevel)) across three saves
[measured]: the game handing its own standing back to
itself, a reward calculation rather than a request for
a mission's difficulty. Recomputing it turned a reward
of 1 into 2.
Matrix offset     MatrixPowerLevelOffset REPLACES the base offset
[measured].
Property names    BasePowerLevelOffset, PowerLevelScalar,
MatrixPowerLevelOffset and teamPowerLevel, the model's
own names.
THERE IS NO FALLBACK SOURCE for Team Power Level. If the instance carries
no readable teamPowerLevel, or carries one that reads 0 - which a freshly
constructed model does before the game fills it in - this subsystem logs
an error and leaves the game's own result alone. It never proceeds on a
default: a default here is not a missing mission difficulty, it is a
silently wrong one.
uiDoc: By default the game clamps mission to a PL of 10. Here, the upper clamp defaults to 20 as enemy archetypes exist up to PL 20. The lower clamp must stay at or below the upper one; set it higher and this refuses to run at all.
Matrix calls have their own upper clamp, so hacking can have its own maximum difficultt. Set it to 0 to use the same clamp for both. Where the two differ, the lower one wins.
The count of logged calculations is also the gate on the check that the mod's Team Power Level agrees with the game's own. Set it to 0 and you lose that check along with the logging.

fields.label: Enable Mission Power Level Ceiling
fields.doc: Slice toggle. It lives in ckf.hardmode.cfg because a gate cannot live inside the file it gates, and the .cfg is parsed before anything else loads. Slices.Init binds every [Slices] key above the [General] Enabled bail-out, so BepInEx writes the line even when the mod is off. A key that cannot be read is reported at Error and treated as on. Off: the subsystem logs why and does nothing this launch. The retired "enabled" key inside the subsystem's JSON file is still parsed (RetiredEnabled) so that Slices.ReportRetiredGate can report it: a Warning, or an Error when it is false and this key is not. Nothing branches on it.
fields.uiDoc: Turn this off and this part of the mod does nothing; the game uses its own values. The master switch on the first page turns off everything at once.

fields.label: Upper clamp
fields.doc: Upper clamp. Stock is 10; enemy archetypes exist through 20. Must not be below minCap - the subsystem refuses to run if it is.

fields.absent: 0 means use maxCap for Matrix calls too.
fields.label: Matrix upper clamp
fields.doc: Separate upper clamp for Matrix calls, so hacking can stay at the stock ceiling while ground missions climb. 0 = use maxCap for both. The lower of this and maxCap wins.

fields.label: Calculations logged
fields.uiDoc: Calculations to log. The cross-check that the mod's Team Power Level matches the game's own is printed inside this gate, so 0 silences the only check that the two agree.

invariants.reason: maxCap below minCap leaves nothing to clamp into; PowerLevelCap.Init logs a warning and does not patch. The keys are spelled file#path because both live at the top level of ckf.hardmode.d/powerlevel.json, which check_schema.py's inv_value reads off disk.
